text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police have confirmed that a Serb was the perpetrator of the killings of two Serbs in Eastern Slavonia over the weekend.
- President Tudjman receives U.N. Transitional Administrator Klein in a farewell visit.
- The deadline for the handing over of weapons in Eastern Slavonia expires on August 19. So far some 3,414 firearms and 848,120 grenades, rockets and launchers have been handed in.

- Croatian Party of Rights (HSP) leader Dobroslav Paraga files a suit before the Hague Tribunal against the Croatian president Tudjman, who he accuses of attacking the neighbouring Bosnia and Herzegovina and Defence Minister Gojko Susak, who he blames for igniting war between the Croat and the Moslem people.
- The electrical goods producer Koncar signs a deal on the selling of the licence for energy transformer production in Malaysia with the local Zanwa company.
- The Adriatic is currently playing host to some half a million tourists, out of that number 370,000 are foreigners.
- IBM breaks the HPT monopoly as Internet provider by offering its services to Croatian clients.
- The number of foreign owners of Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka stocks is on the rise and this brings about speculations of foreign capital soon taking over.
- The sighting of the Adriatic sea-lion was reported to the Pula port authorities on August 5. This is the first such report in a long time as the animal was believed to have become extinct.

- There are speculations that the changes to the Croatian Constitution expected in Autumn may include an item which stipulates that the president of the Constitutional Court is named by the House of Representatives, after a proposal by the president. The Constitution in its current form calls for judges to among themselves choose the individual to fill the post.
- American marines are holding a seminar on stamina training for Croatian Army special troops.
- The recently conducted Croatian work force survey results show that every fifth worker works in agriculture, fishing or forestry. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
